Job Shops Suitable for Electron Beam Welding of Copper Accelerators: OEMs Sciaky and PTR both have job shops in Chicago, Illinois and Enfield, Connecticut respectively. These facilities generally perform shorter term development for customers and run single piece custom parts but are focused more on developing customers for equipment sales. They also suffer from skilled employee attrition as people retire or are offered jobs by their own customers, but due to their deep history of electron beam welding have been able to train the staff required to run their fabrication shops. Pro-Beam is building a centralized US job shop for development but currently uses its German development facilities and US customer facilities. All of these OEMs have a long history of supporting research and development for advanced scientific facilities. There are a number of electron beam welding job shops across the USA but they are not all at the quality level required for electron beam welding of copper accelerators, nor are they all willing to take on work that is single piece or low quantity, and requires high engineering and technician time investment. C.F. Roark (C.F. Roark - C.F. Roark Welding & Engineering Co., Inc. Roark (roarkfab.com)) is an example of a shop that has the high-quality equipment and expertise required to fabricate copper accelerators. Other non-OEM vendors that have these capabilities include: Applied Fusion LLC (The Welding Authority | E-Beam and LASER | Applied Fusion (appliedfusionllc.com)), and Electron Beam Welding Inc. Home - Electron Beam Welding, LLC (electronbeamweldinginc.com). Evaluation metrics and considerations of partners for electron beam welding of copper accelerators: • Personnel o Engineering personnel with skills for design and manufacturing with electron beam welding? o Trades personnel with skills for fabrication with electron beam welding? • Equipment o Can the shop maintain its own equipment? o Located in proximity to or have strong relationship with OEM? Economics of an Electron Beam Welding Job Shop Due to the very high capital investment required for electron beam welding systems and the required support equipment, businesses need to ensure steady flow of work or risk going bankrupt.
